summary: Generates staggered 0-to-1 easing phases across multiple samples for time-offset animation interpolation.
key_concepts: Phaser CHOP generates staggered phaser values between 0 and 1 for groups of animated samples or channels.
The first input is a single 0-to-1 control channel that drives the start-to-end cycle.
The optional second input supplies explicit per-sample phase positions; otherwise phases are distributed uniformly.
Edge controls how sharply separated or cohesive the staggered group is, with small values making sharper transitions.
Output Format chooses between multiple samples in one channel and multiple output channels.
Lookup CHOP is commonly used after Phaser CHOP to map the 0-to-1 phase values into animated channel groups.

key_params.name: edge
key_params.note: Controls cohesiveness/transition width of staggered group

key_params.name: samples
key_params.note: Output multiple samples in a channel

key_params.name: channels
key_params.note: Number of output channels when relevant

key_params.name: extend
key_params.note: Clamp, cycle, or mirror slope behavior

key_params.name: mirrorslope
key_params.note: Mirror phase and flip the slope

key_params.name: add
key_params.note: Continue increasing or decreasing outside the 0-to-1 input range

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: The first input is expected to be one channel with values between 0 and 1 controlling the start-to-end cycle.
The output is one channel with multiple samples by default; each sample has a staggered easing phase.
The second input optionally supplies irregular phase values, typically N samples between 0 and 1.
Without a phase input, per-sample phase is distributed uniformly as i/N.
Use Lookup CHOP after Phaser CHOP to map 0-1 phase values into groups of animated channels.
Edge values strongly affect whether objects transition quickly and separately or slowly/in unison.
